name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP)
summary: A credit-linked margin money subsidy for setting up new micro-enterprises in the non-farm sector, with the rest of the project cost financed by a bank term loan. UNVERIFIED: the current revised guidelines could not be opened on 6 October 2026, so age, education and new-unit conditions come from an older published copy of the guidelines; whether the scheme continues after 2025-26 is not confirmed.
benefits: Margin money subsidy of 15% (urban) or 25% (rural) of the project cost for general category applicants

Margin money subsidy of 25% (urban) or 35% (rural) of the project cost for special category applicants (SC, ST, OBC, women, transgender, physically disabled, North Eastern Region, aspirational and border district applicants)
Maximum project cost of ₹50 lakh for manufacturing units and ₹20 lakh for service units (raised from ₹25 lakh and ₹10 lakh in the 2022 revision)
The balance of the project cost is provided by a bank as a term loan
Older guidelines: beneficiary's own contribution of 10% of the project cost (general) or 5% (special category); check the current figure
implementing_agency: Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), with State KVIBs, District Industries Centres and banks
ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises

rules.label: Applicant is a self-help group, production co-operative society or charitable trust (the age rule applies to individuals)
Individual applicant is above 18 years of age
Assistance is for new projects only; existing units are not eligible
rules.sourceRef: KVIC PMEGP guidelines (older copy), para 4 and 4.1(v)

rules.label: The unit has not already availed a government subsidy under any other Central or State scheme
Project is in the manufacturing sector
Project cost is at most ₹50 lakh for a manufacturing unit
Project is in the service or business sector
Project cost is at most ₹20 lakh for a service or business unit
At least VIII standard pass (needed for larger projects)
Manufacturing project
Manufacturing project costing up to ₹10 lakh needs no minimum education
Service or business project
Service or business project costing up to ₹5 lakh needs no minimum education

how_to_apply: Apply online on the PMEGP e-portal; applications are handled by KVIC, a State KVIB or a District Industries Centre and the loan is sanctioned by a bank. Published but not evaluated here: only one person from a family (self and spouse) is eligible, and the portal was not reachable when this entry was prepared, so check its current guidelines.

sources.title: PIB: Continuation of PMEGP over the 15th Finance Commission cycle, 2021-22 to 2025-26 (30 May 2022)
KVIC: PMEGP guidelines (older copy; project-cost limits have since been raised)

name: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY)
summary: Loans up to ₹10 lakh (up to ₹20 lakh under Tarun Plus, for entrepreneurs who have availed and successfully repaid previous loans in the Tarun category) to non-corporate, non-farm small and micro enterprises, given by banks, RRBs, small finance banks, MFIs and NBFCs. MUDRA refinances these lenders and does not lend directly. Not evaluated here: that the enterprise is non-farm and small or micro, and whether an earlier Tarun loan was repaid.
benefits: Shishu: loans up to ₹50,000
Kishor: loans above ₹50,000 and up to ₹5 lakh
Tarun: loans above ₹5 lakh and up to ₹10 lakh
Tarun Plus: loans above ₹10 lakh and up to ₹20 lakh, for entrepreneurs who have availed and successfully repaid previous loans under the Tarun category
Loans are given by commercial banks, RRBs, small finance banks, MFIs and NBFCs
implementing_agency: Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency (MUDRA), through banks, RRBs, small finance banks, MFIs and NBFCs

rules.label: The enterprise is non-corporate
Loan sought is up to ₹10 lakh, or up to ₹20 lakh under Tarun Plus (only for entrepreneurs who repaid an earlier Tarun loan)

how_to_apply: Approach a commercial bank, RRB, small finance bank, MFI or NBFC, or apply online on the Udyami Mitra portal (udyamimitra.in). Agents or middlemen are not engaged by MUDRA for Mudra loans.

sources.title: MUDRA: PMMY home page (read 6 October 2026; loan categories and Tarun Plus note)

name: Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE)
summary: A guarantee cover for collateral-free and/or third-party-guarantee-free credit that eligible lenders extend to new or existing micro and small enterprises. The enterprise applies to a lender, not to CGTMSE, and the Trust can accept or reject a proposal. The credit facility cap is ₹10 crore for banks and select financial institutions, ₹2 crore for RRBs, small finance banks, state financial institutions and co-operative banks, and ₹50 lakh for microfinance institutions. Not evaluated here: that the borrower is a micro or small enterprise.
benefits: Guarantee cover on term loan and/or working capital facilities given without collateral or third-party guarantee, up to ₹10 crore per borrower
Hybrid option: the lender may take collateral for part of a facility and the unsecured part, up to ₹10 crore, can be covered
Trading (retail or wholesale) and educational or training institutions are eligible activities
Higher extent of guarantee cover for women entrepreneurs, SC/ST entrepreneurs, persons with disability and MSEs in the North East, Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh (see the scheme document)
Annual guarantee fee reduced to a minimum of 0.37% per annum
implementing_agency: Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE), through Member Lending Institutions
ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises

required.label: Credit facility does not exceed ₹10 crore (₹2 crore or ₹50 lakh for some types of lender)

how_to_apply: Approach a Member Lending Institution (a bank, NBFC or financial institution registered with CGTMSE) for an MSE loan without collateral; the lender requests the guarantee cover. CGTMSE does not lend directly.

sources.title: CGTMSE: Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGS-I) scheme document, updated as on 1 April 2025

name: PM Vishwakarma
summary: Support for artisans and craftspeople in 18 family-based traditional trades: recognition, skill training with a stipend, a toolkit incentive, collateral-free credit in two tranches at a concessional interest rate, and an incentive for digital transactions. Not evaluated here: the 18 listed trades, registration limited to one family member, and the rule that a person who took a loan under a similar Central or State scheme (such as PMEGP, PM SVANidhi or Mudra) in the past 5 years is not eligible unless a Mudra or SVANidhi loan was fully repaid. The portal reports its registration target of 30,00,000 as reached in September 2025, so confirm that registration is open.
benefits: Recognition as a Vishwakarma
Basic training of 5-7 days (40 hours) with a stipend of ₹500 per day; optional advanced training of 15 days (120 hours)
Toolkit incentive of up to ₹15,000
Collateral-free credit of up to ₹1 lakh (18-month repayment), then up to ₹2 lakh (30-month repayment) in a second tranche after the first is repaid; ₹3 lakh in total
Concessional interest of 5% charged to the beneficiary; the Government of India bears the interest subvention (capped at 8%) and the credit guarantee fee
Incentive of ₹1 per digital transaction, up to 100 transactions a month
Marketing support through the National Committee for Marketing
implementing_agency: Ministry of MSME, with the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and the Department of Financial Services
ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises

rules.label: An artisan or craftsperson working with hands and tools in one of the 18 family-based traditional trades, self-employed in the unorganised sector
At least 18 years of age on the date of registration
Neither the person nor a family member is in government service

how_to_apply: Register on the PM Vishwakarma portal (applicant login, or through a Common Service Centre). The first credit tranche follows skill assessment and basic training.

sources.title: PM Vishwakarma portal home page: eligibility and benefits (read 6 October 2026)

name: Stand-Up India Scheme
summary: RETIRED. The Department of Financial Services page states that the scheme ran up to 31 March 2025, in line with the 15th Finance Commission cycle, and mentions a new scheme for first-time women, SC and ST entrepreneurs (term loans up to ₹2 crore) announced in Budget 2025-26. No later extension was found on the official sources read on 6 October 2026, although the Stand-Up India portal still shows the original scheme features. Kept for reference; its published criteria are encoded below. Not evaluated here: for non-individual enterprises, at least 51% of shareholding and control must be held by an SC/ST or woman entrepreneur.
benefits: Composite bank loan (term loan plus working capital) between ₹10 lakh and ₹1 crore
Loan expected to cover 85% of the project cost; promoter margin money of 15%, with at least 10% of the project cost as the borrower's own contribution
Repayment in up to 7 years with a moratorium of up to 18 months
Security cover under the Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme for Stand-Up India Loans (CGFSIL), or collateral, as decided by the bank
implementing_agency: Scheduled commercial banks, with the Stand-Up India portal run by SIDBI
ministry: Ministry of Finance (Department of Financial Services)

rules.label: Woman entrepreneur
Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe entrepreneur
Above 18 years of age
Loans are for a greenfield project only: the borrower's first-time venture
The borrower is not in default to any bank or financial institution
Composite loan between ₹10 lakh and ₹1 crore
rules.sourceRef: standupmitra.in, Scheme Features: Nature and Size of Loan

how_to_apply: Retired scheme: no application route is listed. Ask a bank branch or check the official sources about the successor scheme for first-time women, SC and ST entrepreneurs.
